module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjectures associated with A109908

$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.

*References:*
- [A109908](https://oeis.org/A109908)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA109908

/--
$a(n)$ = greatest prime of the form $k(n-k)-1$, or $0$ if no such prime exists.
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 (n / 2))
  |>.image (fun k => k * (n - k) - 1)
  |>.filter Nat.Prime
  |>.sup id

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 3 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by decide

/--
Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for $n > 3$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture : ∀ n > 3, a n > 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA109908

reformulations.difference: The prose definition is implemented by searching only 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊n/2⌋, rather than the full range 1 ≤ k < n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The substitution k ↦ n−k preserves k(n−k)−1 and moves every upper-half candidate into the lower half. I proved equality of the two finite candidate sets and their filtered prime maxima in Lean for every natural n. I also verified that both natural-number subtractions agree with integer subtraction throughout the candidate range. Finset.sup returns the greatest candidate, or 0 when the prime set is empty. OEIS's own Maple and PARI programs likewise use the half-range.

sources_consulted: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A109/A109908.seq — official OEIS entry, including definition, conjecture, verification remark, programs, and offset
https://oeis.org/A109908/b109908.txt — Robert Israel's published term table
review.notes: All seven declarations were checked. The conjecture matches OEIS exactly: a(n) > 0 for n > 3. The entry still calls it a conjecture and records verification up to 10^9, consistent with the research-open tag. All five test theorems match the source; an additional Lean computation matched all first 200 published terms. Boundary cases n = 0, 1, 2, 3 yield an empty prime set and value 0. Scratch proofs and tests are in /workspace/review/. The main OEIS page was blocked by Cloudflare, so its full entry was read through the official OEIS data mirror.
